podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Great Trilogy" - Early Career Definition
podcast.body: The most recognized and legendary period of Michael Field's career is considered to be his beginning, between the ages of 17 and 20, when he released a "great trilogy" of albums. This era, encompassing "Tubular Bells" (1973) and "Ommadawn" (1975), was crucial for him to progressively define his unique musical sound. "la parte más conocida o la parte más mítica de Michael Field es precisamente el inicio de su carrera cuando apenas tenía 17, 20 años, cuando saca esa gran trilogía."

podcast.title: Anti-Electronic and Digital Stance
podcast.body: In the era of 1990, when "Amarok" was released, Michael Field was a staunch opponent of electronic instruments, electronic music, and digital production methods. This aversion dictated the album's production, which entirely utilized "old school" systems, a choice considered truly admirable given the technological trends of the time. "Michael Field en esa época era un grandísimo atacante de todos los instrumentos electrónicos y de la música electrónica, incluso era un gran atacante de la producción digital."

srcs.episode: Mike Oldfield - Amarok. ¿Es su mejor disco?

podcast.title: Defiance of Virgin Records with Amarok
podcast.body: Michael Field created "Amarok" partly as an expression of his frustration and anger with Virgin Records, who had spent years pressuring him to produce a "Tubular Bells 2." Although he never entirely dismissed the idea of a sequel, he was profoundly dissatisfied with his relationship with Virgin Records, openly criticizing both Richard Branson and the label in various interviews, and believing Virgin's actions in the 1980s negatively impacted his discographic quality. "fue una hora hecha por Michael Field, y para la mala leche o el cabrero que tenía con Virging."

podcast.title: Early Start & Autodidacticism
podcast.body: Michael Field began his musical career at the age of 15, entirely self-taught, forging his own path as a musician. "empezó ya con 15 años, completamente autodidacta, he hecho a sí mismo."

podcast.title: Influences in Early Career
podcast.body: Across his first three albums, including "Tubular Bells" and "Ommadawn," Michael Field gradually shaped his sound by exploring and incorporating a wide array of new instruments and sonic textures. His influences during this period included distinct elements such as Celtic music and the rhythmic patterns of African drums. "va cogiendo influencias de cosas como de la música Celta, ritmos de tambores africanos, muchas cosas que va incorporando poco a poco en esos tres discos."

podcast.title: Relationship with Richard Branson & Virgin Records
podcast.body: Michael Field's relationship with Richard Branson and Virgin Records was notably contentious, described as being almost "at loggerheads." Despite this difficult dynamic, Virgin Records and Richard Branson owe a significant portion of their success and fortune to the immense commercial impact of Michael Field's "Tubular Bells." "Virgin, le debe gran parte de su fortuna, porque el gran éxito de Virgin como discográfica se la debe al éxito de Michael Field."

srcs.episode: Mike Oldfield - Amarok. ¿Es su mejor disco?

podcast.title: Solo Recording and Virtuosity
podcast.body: "Amarok" was recorded almost entirely by Michael Field alone, who played dozens of instruments masterfully and largely self-produced the album, with only minor punctual assistance from a producer. The resulting sound is astonishingly rich, giving the impression of an enormous band or even an orchestra of 30-50 musicians who have rigorously rehearsed for years, serving as a testament to his exceptional musical virtuosity. "Michael Field lo graba totalmente solo, el toca todos los instrumentos a algo una pequeña sección puntual, se graba a sí mismo, prácticamente se produce a sí mismo."
